scope: Classify and record workflow/task failure dispositions without dispatching work, retrying providers, reconciling providers, mutating canonical manuscript state, cancelling/resuming jobs or executing Book admission.
laws: Every observed failure is bound to exact workflow, plan, source and task identity and receives an explicit disposition; unknown failure classes fail closed.
A required task may never be silently dropped after failure, abstention, rejection, missing evidence or unresolved authority.
A task marked not required for plan success may continue as partial only when no required downstream task depends on it through a required dependency edge.
If any required downstream task depends on a failed optional task, the failure blocks that downstream path and becomes FAIL_CLOSED_REQUIRED_TASK.
Provider timeout or other unknown outcome must route through Phase 2F operation identity and retry/reconciliation rules; the failure layer does not perform retry or reconciliation.
An idempotent provider unknown outcome may disposition RETRY_POLICY_REQUIRED; a non-idempotent provider unknown outcome dispositions RECONCILIATION_REQUIRED.
Missing required evidence fails closed even if the provider reported SUCCESS or PARTIAL elsewhere.
Stale manuscript/source/plan or stale context invalidates the current execution attempt; no old candidate may advance toward admission.
Hard-gate failure preserves the original and prohibits canonical effect from the rejected candidate.
Unresolved author or other required authority waits rather than being synthesized or bypassed.
Declared-but-unavailable capability interfaces remain explicit blockers; they are never replaced with guessed providers.
Book admission rejection leaves canonical manuscript state unchanged and cannot be reclassified as provider success.
Failure records contain hashes/references and bounded codes only; raw manuscript/candidate text is forbidden.
A failure disposition can never itself mark a workflow COMPLETED_ADMITTED or mutate canonical manuscript state.
Original manuscript recoverability is a hard invariant for every failure disposition.
